Cooking

The cook loop — server-of-truth sessions from idempotency-keyed start to two-write completion: step progress, long-prep stages, the ONE shared per-session timer rendered by three surfaces, raw-binary photos, the log draft, and the completion that publishes CookedMealCreated and writes leftovers back into the pantry. Flow3 (bought → cookable notification) is the named NOT-BUILT gap — the forward plan's first born-red candidate.

Docs The feature card

the entity in one handle, one analogy and one constraint box

Authored in cards/cooking.md — the only hand-written source on this page. Everything counted elsewhere is read from the codebase at build time.

“"The kitchen's active orders board — the server owns every ticket, every timer, every 'done'."”

ISthe session lifecycle (start/steps/stages/readiness/timer/complete/cancel), cook photos, the cook log, dish history, and the cooking-timer notification machinery.
IS NOTrecipe browse/detail (the catalog the cook starts from) and not what completion TRIGGERS downstream — skills and progression recompute in their own entities off the event.
DECIDESwhether a cook may start (allergen 403, concurrent cap 409, idempotency replay), which step/stage a session is on, when the one timer fires, what completion records (actual vs stored portions), and what survives a cancel (nothing — photos wiped, timer cleared).

a restaurant expo station — one ticket rail (active sessions, capped), each ticket carrying its own single timer bell, a photo clip per ticket, and a strict close-out ritual: count portions eaten vs stored, stamp the ledger, ring the back office (events), and shelve the leftovers with a use-by date.

AnalogyIn this codebase
ticket railapps/api/services/cooking.py:107, :152 (cap table :74)
timer bellservices/cooking.py:419-499, services/notifications.py:101
close-out ritualservices/cooking.py:544, api/cooking.py:417
photo clipapi/cooking.py:469-561
back officeevents/bus.py:60, :94-107

Easy to confuse:

  • the browse screen is ALSO called CookingScreen — its session part is only the active-cook section; the rest is the recipe entity's browse surface.
  • the 409s — concurrent-cook cap (api/cooking.py:164) vs allergen 403 (:159): capacity vs safety, different doors.

Where the analogy stops working: the expo analogy breaks on the cap — it is deliberately SOFT (non-atomic count, services/cooking.py:196); two simultaneous starts can both pass. It is UX guidance, not a quota wall.

Full card — what & why, for whom, flows, is / is not

What & Why

Cooking is where a recipe becomes a cooked meal (SCOPE REQ-03). A session starts against the wall and the cap — Idempotency-Key required (400 without, api/cooking.py:119), allergen-gated (403), concurrent-cook capped per tier (free 3 / chef 20, one bucket since H6, services/cooking.py:74-86) — and from then on the SERVER owns the state: step completion is an upsert keyed (session, step) with an IDOR guard (:255-263), long-prep advances by compare-and-set stage with due reminders (services/long_prep.py:107, :66), and readiness merges source/photo/mode plus a 4 KB log_draft the web debounces in (api/cooking.py:332; CookingFlowContainer.tsx:505). H7 gives each session at most ONE timer — timer_step_id/timer_ends_at on the row (models/cooking.py:85-86, server clock authority) — whose scheduling writes a due_at notification (services/notifications.py:101) and whose replacement/cancel/completion clears the pending one (:130). Three surfaces render that single deadline: the active cards' TimerBadge, modo receta's step button (an ownsSharedTimer window), and modo cocina's controls. Completion is a guarded two-write ritual: the web's portions gate (ateAll → leftover → stored, CookingLogPortionsGate) feeds a validated CompletionRequest (stored ≤ actual, schemas/cooking.py:122); the service replays idempotently if already completed (:576), snapshots the recipe into DishHistoryEvent (:659), writes a prepared pantry item with storage-method expiry when stored > 0 (:600), and only after commit publishes CookedMealCreated (api/cooking.py:417) — the bus runs each subscriber in its own SAVEPOINT and swallows failures, which is why every handler downstream is an idempotent recompute (events/bus.py:30-87). Cancel is total: status cancelled, photos deleted, timer and pending notifications cleared (:209-249).

For Whom

  • The cook mid-dish — greasy-fingered, phone-locked, tab-closed: the server remembers the step, the timer, the photos, and the half-written note; any surface picks up exactly where they left off.
  • The multi-day cook — long-prep stages with come-back-later reminders that fire when due, not when the app happens to be open.
  • The household — up to the cap of simultaneous pots; each pane of the in-cook pager is one live session.
  • The progression engine and skill ledger — completion is their ONLY input signal; the event contract (publish-after-commit, idempotent recompute) is what lets them trust it.

Flows

  • start → POST /cooking/sessions (api/cooking.py:114): Idempotency-Key required, 404 recipe / 403 allergen / 409 cap; replay returns the existing session. (assured: test_cooking + test_cooking_concurrent_cap in the api corpus)
  • cook ★ → step upsert (PATCH .../steps/{id}), long-prep CAS stage advance + due reminders, readiness merge incl. the debounced log_draft; the in-cook pager panes live+pinned sessions (H6). (assured: the cook-state journey C-cases — steps survive reload, ongoing detail, draft persist; proof set cook-state, 14 files)
  • timer → PATCH .../timer (H7): one per session — start/replace/clear; ends_at = now + duration on the server clock; schedules the due_at notification "Paso N: título"; replace/cancel/complete clears the pending one. Three surfaces render the one deadline. (assured: test_cooking_timer, 17 cases)
  • photos → PUT/GET/DELETE .../photos/{slot} (H8): raw binary slots (initial | step-N), 409 at the cap, ETag/304 reads; web compresses to 1600px JPEG and strips EXIF first (photoCompression.ts:109). (assured: test_cooking_photos, 17 cases)
  • complete → the two-step portions gate (web) → validated CompletionRequest → idempotent completion: DishHistoryEvent with recipe_snapshot, prepared pantry write-back when stored>0 (D121 shelf life), consumption events (source="receta"), CookedMealCreated published after commit. (assured: test_cooking completion cases + cookingStorageMethod.test.ts)
  • cancel → POST .../cancel: the N1-unified confirm on both cook modes guards it; server wipes photos, clears timer + pending notifications, status cancelled.
  • exit → the completion log's ✕ (D180-3): it asks instead of deciding. One popup names all three ways out — save the registro (with the portion count it will store), continue later (session stays resumable, nothing written), or cancel the recipe — and ✕/Escape/backdrop returns to the form having written nothing. The save row runs the SAME submit as the primary CTA, so what the button promises and what reaches the pantry cannot diverge. (assured: the exitPrompt wiring guard, mutation-proven in both directions)
  • notify-not-built → Flow3 (bought → cookable notification) does NOT exist: no pantry-change bus event, no cookability-delta recompute, no notification category, no demands link (adoption.json flows). The forward plan's first born-red candidate — /gabe-plan the phase, /gabe-red declares its C-ids, then /gabe-execute.

Is

  • Server-of-truth state: completed_step_ids from the server is the truth the web renders (cookingSessionModel.ts:137); optimistic grafts are cache conveniences, invalidated wide on completion.
  • One timer per session, by schema: two nullable columns on the row — not a timers table; the xor guard (both-or-neither) lives in the request validator and the service (:441).
  • Idempotent at both ends: start replays by (household, idempotency_key) unique; completion replays by unique session_id on DishHistoryEvent (models/cooking.py:135).
  • Publish-after-commit + savepoint isolation: a failing subscriber can never roll back a completed cook, and a dropped handler self-heals on the next recompute — the reason downstream is recompute-never-increment.
  • The cap is soft by design (services/cooking.py:196): a non-atomic count keeps start cheap; a racing pair can land cap+1.
  • Cancel leaves no residue: photos, timer, pending notifications all cleared in one service call.
  • The exit control asks, it never decides (D180-3): pressing ✕ on the completion log opens a popup naming every way out rather than silently picking one. Leaving is non-destructive by construction — the session stays resumable and nothing is written — so no exit affordance performs an irreversible pantry write.
  • The log is now read by someone else (F6/D187): cocinadas on a repertorio cupo is a query over DishHistoryEvent by dish type + actor — the cooking entity writes the log, the recipe entity reads it, and nothing about a cupo writes back here. That is why releasing a cupo cannot erase a cook: the count was never the cupo's to hold.
  • One number, two places it appears: the popup's save row reads the same effectiveStoredPortions the completion request sends, so the count on the button is the count that reaches the pantry. When nothing is stored the "+ N" clause is absent rather than promising portions that will not arrive.
  • not a screen whose buttons are all wired — the browse empty state offered "Agregar ingrediente" with no handler from the S24b seam until P5b, and its ERROR-state twin still does: "Reintentar" and "Ver guardadas" both render as full buttons with no onClick, so the screen a user only reaches when something already went wrong offers two exits and neither works (filed #200, deliberately not fixed alongside #172 — that finding named one button).

Is Not

  • not the browse/detail surface — the recipe entity owns the catalog the cook starts from, including the screen file both share.
  • not skills/progression — those entities subscribe to CookedMealCreated; this card ends at the publish site.
  • not the pantry — the prepared-leftover write-back crosses into pantry territory deliberately (D121); the pantry card owns the expiry rendering.
  • not push notifications — the timer notification is a due_at row the client polls (GET /cooking/reminders/due; 60s poll in useRemindersDue); no push transport exists.

Docs Changelog — decisions that shaped it

why the entity behaves the way it does

Source: the entity card's DECIDED section. A decision here is a rule the code obeys, not a plan — the ones with ids are in .kdbp/DECISIONS.md.

DecisionWhat it settles
H6mixing removed: one cap bucket (free 3 / chef 20), pager panes per live session; the combined-cook allergen guard ceased to exist.
H7the shared server timer: one per session on the row, server-clock ends_at, due_at notification rows, three rendering surfaces, cleared on replace/cancel/complete.
H8photos are raw binary slots on the session (initial | step-N), capped, ETag/304 served; the web compresses + strips EXIF before upload.
N1one confirm primitive: cancel confirms on both cook modes thin-wrap the shared ConfirmDialog molecule.
—The two-step completion gate (founder redesign): ateAll → leftover → storedPortions before the request is buildable; stored ≤ actual validated server-side.
D180-1bthe per-person discount PROPOSES, it never post-processes: the household's servings seed the gate's opening state (eaten = min(people, made), stored = max(0, made − eaten)), so the cook confirms a number rather than doing arithmetic. Applying it after the gate was built and reverted — the gate's stored count is already net of eating, so discounting again subtracted the same meal twice. There is no third question: exposing our own bookkeeping to someone who was standing at the stove is a defect class, not a feature.
D180-3bthe ✕ asks; founder rule 2 is SUPERSEDED, not implemented: rule 2 said closing the log carries what was made forward as stored. What it protected against — the food exists and we lose track of it — is already prevented by resumability, which did not exist in its current form when the rule was written. The narrower real defect was a bare glyph that could not say it was non-destructive. Rejected on the way: relabelling the ✕ (honest about only one of the two exits) and writing to the pantry from an exit control (a no-undo dead-end on the way OUT of a flow).
—Publish-after-commit + savepoint-isolated, swallowed handlers — the event contract that forces downstream recompute-never-increment.
Soft concurrent capnon-atomic by documented design (services/cooking.py:196).
D121stored leftovers become prepared pantry items with storage-method shelf life at completion time.

Code Data model

DB entities and API shapes — each names its file and the endpoints that touch it

A field typed with another documented class LINKS to it (violet) instead of repeating its structure. Examples are synthetic — derived from Literal values and field-name heuristics, never real user data.
Type colors — one hue per family, deeper = the wider type: int float · Decimal numeric · date · time datetime temporal · str bytes · Text textual · bool · list · dict · Literal structured · UUID identity · None nullable. An uncolored token is a domain alias (an enum defined in this codebase).
Insight icons — the DATA-MODEL lens; the same shape runs over other member kinds later (functions · methods), scoped, never mixed:
  • model — a persisted DB entity: lives in a table, owns FKs.
  • schema — an API / pipeline shape: crosses a boundary, owns no storage.
  • base — derives from NOTHING: no FK out, no field typed by another documented class; a foundation others build on.
  • N god-class flag — field count ≥ 15; the number that makes it a split candidate below.
  • Class N% closest structural twin — % = shared fields over the union (Jaccard); a ≥80% pair becomes a merge candidate below.
  • Usage bars: teal = api (endpoint touches + FK in) · violet = internal (mapped backend files referencing the class). Both bars are EVIDENCE, never a verdict: they count references inside the config-mapped files only, so a zero means no indexed usage — go check, never dead. One unmapped file falsifies a zero; nothing falsifies a count.

About this section

The API surface is api/cooking.py (sessions/steps/stages/readiness/timer/complete/cancel/photos/reminders). Services: services/cooking.py (lifecycle + cap + timer + the two-write completion), services/long_prep.py (stage schedule + CAS + due reminders), services/notifications.py (due_at scheduling + pending-clear + the poll read), services/cooking_photos.py (slot storage), services/dish_history.py (the read model). Data: models/cooking.py (CookingSession + step progress + DishHistoryEvent + stage reminders + photos), models/notification.py (Notification.due_at + ProfileProjection). Events: events/types.py (CookedMealCreated) + events/bus.py (savepoint-isolated publish, register_handlers). The web core is CookingFlowContainer.tsx (per-cook flow: timer seed, log-draft debounce, completion), cookingSessionModel.ts (pure mappers), useCookingSessions.ts (the hook family incl. useSetSessionTimer's targeted graft), inCookPanes.ts + components/inCookPagerModel.ts (H6 pager math), model/CookingScreenModel.ts, components/log/CookingLogComponents.tsx (the portions gate), photoCompression.ts, and the three timer surfaces (components/active/ActiveCookingCards.tsx, screens/RecipeDetailScreen.tsx modo receta, screens/CookingModeScreen.tsx + components/mode/CookingModeComponents.tsx).

Code Data-model candidates

MERGE and SPLIT — named by the machine, ruled by judgment; the verdict lands in DECISIONS/PENDING via review or a health pass, never here

What the candidate icons mean
  • merge — structural twins ≥ 80% (from the similarity flag).
  • split — a god class ≥ 15 fields (from the N fields flag).
Why these two, and not "nothing uses this" — similarity and size are CORPUS-COMPLETE signals: two mapped classes sharing 87% of their field names is TRUE no matter what lives outside the map, and a 22-field class is 22 fields however little the config covers. Absence of references is neither — a single file outside the entity config falsifies it. This section names only what the instrument can actually support. The usage evidence lives on the Data model page — two bars per class, api and internal — and a reader checks it there.
The floor, stated honestly — the similarity flag records the TOP-1 nearest neighbour per class only, only above the 50% line, Python only, mapped files only, and only field NAMES (types and semantics are not compared). Every one of those is a way to MISS a pair, never a way to invent one. This TABLE cuts higher still — it lists pairs at ≥ 80%, so the 50% recording floor is what the flag sees, not what you are reading. This page is a FLOOR, not a census: it under-reports duplication and always will. That direction is the safe one — under-reporting a positive signal costs you a missed merge; under-reporting absence gets live code deleted.
Known blind spot — classes outside the entity config are invisible here, and the misses cluster there rather than in the maths: two modules can carry near-identical schemas and drift apart for months without either appearing on this page, if one of them is not in the config. An empty candidates table means the mapped set is clean, not the repository.

every def in this entity's mapped backend files — the FUNCTIONS lens, sibling of the data model above

Insight icons — the FUNCTIONS lens:
  • function — a module-level def.
  • method — a def bound to a class.
  • endpoint handler — a route decorator serves it.
  • base — calls no other documented function; a foundation others build on.
  • N god-function flag — length ≥ 50 lines; makes it a split candidate below.
  • fn N% closest structural twin — body-identifier overlap (Jaccard); a ≥85% pair becomes a merge candidate below.
  • Usage bars: teal = api (endpoints served + api-layer files referencing) · violet = internal (mapped files referencing — same-file calls outside the def count: a helper used within its module is used). Both bars are EVIDENCE, never a verdict: the scan reads config-mapped Python only, so a zero reads no indexed caller — go check, never dead.

Code Function candidates

MERGE and SPLIT — named by the machine, ruled by judgment; same contract as the data-model candidates, function-scoped

What the candidate icons mean
  • merge — identifier twins ≥ 85% (from the similarity flag).
  • split — a god function ≥ 50 lines (from the N length flag).
Why these two, and not "nothing calls this" — similarity and length are CORPUS-COMPLETE signals: two mapped defs sharing 87% of their body identifiers is TRUE regardless of what lies outside the map, and a 120-line function is 120 lines however little the config covers. "Nothing references this" is falsified by one file outside the corpus — so this section names duplication and size, and never asserts deadness. The usage evidence lives on the Functions page — two bars per def, api and internal — and a reader checks it there.
The floor, stated honestly — the similarity flag records the TOP-1 nearest neighbour per def, only among defs with ≥ 8 body identifiers, only above the 60% line, Python only, mapped files only — while this TABLE cuts higher still, listing pairs at ≥ 85%. Every one of those is a way to MISS a pair, never a way to invent one. The page is a FLOOR, not a census — and that direction is the safe one: under-reporting a positive signal costs a missed merge, while under-reporting absence gets live code deleted.
Known blind spot — files outside the entity config are invisible here, and the misses cluster there rather than in the maths: two modules can share dozens of byte-identical functions and drift apart for months without either appearing on this page, if one of them is not in the config. An empty candidates table means the mapped set is clean, not the repository.
